description: Lets make the way out of this procrastination
summary:
Colony: Moon → Mars → Titan is a 2D sandbox survival game, inspired by Terraria, that lets players practice the problems astronauts face when settling other worlds. Instead of a pickaxe, players use a battery-powered drill, and they must manage an oxygen supply and energy while exploring. Each planet has its own gravity (Moon 1.62, Mars 3.71, Titan 1.35 m/s²) and its own hazards: day–night cycles, Martian dust storms that cut solar power, and Titan’s extreme cold.

To advance, players must build a regolith-shielded dome, an oxygen generator that uses water ice, and solar panels, then make rocket fuel from ice before flying to the next planet. This mirrors real in-situ resource utilization: future crews are expected to produce oxygen, fuel and shelter from local ice and regolith instead of shipping everything from Earth.

The game is important because it turns abstract space-colonization challenges into hands-on decisions about survival, resources and planning, helping students and the public understand what living off Earth requires. It is a simplified prototype, not a training simulator.
details:
Colony: Moon → Mars → Titan is a browser-based 2D survival and building game in the style of Terraria. The player is an astronaut who drills into the ground, collects regolith, ice and metal ore, and builds a working colony. A level is complete only when the colony works: a regolith-shielded dome, an oxygen generator inside it, and solar panels. The crew then turns eight units of ice into rocket fuel and launches to the next world.

How it works. Terrain is generated for each planet, with craters and buried ice and ore. The astronaut has an oxygen tank and a battery. Oxygen drains outside and is refilled at the lander, or inside the dome once an oxygen generator is built. The drill runs on battery energy, and solar panels recharge it by day. If oxygen runs out, the crew is evacuated to the lander and loses half the cargo. Each planet changes the rules. Real gravity (Moon 1.62, Mars 3.71, Titan 1.35 m/s²) changes jumping and climbing. On the Moon, ice lies deep underground. Mars has dust storms that cut solar power by 70%. Titan’s cold makes the suit use more energy.

Benefits and intended impact. Players learn by making decisions rather than reading facts. They see why a base needs power, air and shelter, and why crews are expected to use local resources instead of shipping everything from Earth. The game needs no installation and works on desktop and touch devices, so students, teachers and anyone curious about space settlement can try it.

Tools. HTML5 Canvas, JavaScript and CSS in a single file with no external libraries. The demo slides were built with pptxgenjs. No special hardware is needed. The game code and slides were created with AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic).

Creativity. The usual sandbox tools are replaced with realistic ones, such as a powered drill and a limited oxygen supply. Building the colony is the key to progress, and each planet teaches a different adaptation problem.

Factors considered. We balanced realism against playability: the day length is compressed, the dome is a simplified pressurized zone, and radiation is represented only by the shielding layer. We also considered accessibility, making each planet feel different but fair, and an honest scope: this is an educational prototype, not a validated training tool.
